Article Title: JD(U) extends full support to delimitation, women's reservation proposals
Article Text:
The Janata Dal (United) has voiced its endorsement for the upcoming Constitution amendment bills focused on delimitation and women's reservation.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Janata Dal (United) on Saturday announced its full support for the proposed Constitution amendment bills on delimitation and women's reservation, calling them a significant step towards strengthening Indian democracy.In a post on X, JD(U) working president Sanjay Kumar Jha said the proposal envisages a 50 per cent increase in the existing strength of the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies, while paving the way for 33 per cent reservation for women in these bodies."The Janata Dal (United) fully supports this proposal," Jha said, describing it as an important initiative to expand Indian democracy.He said the proposed increase in the number of seats would broaden people's representation and create greater opportunities for women's participation in the decision-making process, reported by news agency PTI.Jha also urged political parties to set aside their differences and extend support to the bills, calling for a constructive role in ensuring their passage in parliament through a broad consensus.Meanwhile, the BJP-led Centre is preparing to introduce a fresh constitution amendment bill in the Lok Sabha on Monday.The legislation seeks to implement 33 per cent reservation for women by increasing the number of seats in the Lok Sabha, state assemblies and Union Territory legislatures by 50 per cent.It also proposes to freeze the revised seat allocations and constituency boundaries until 2051.The constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, proposes to increase the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha from its existing limit to 850 members. This would include up to 815 representatives from states and 35 from Union territories.The legislation also seeks to raise the maximum strength of state legislative assemblies from 500 to 650 members.According to the bill's statement of objects and reasons, the proposed changes aim to implement one-third reservation for women, including those belonging to scheduled castes (SCs) and scheduled tribes (STs), in the Lok Sabha and state and union territory legislative assemblies through a delimitation exercise.
Article Summary: The BJP-led Centre is preparing to introduce a fresh constitution amendment bill in the Lok Sabha on Monday. The legislation seeks to implement 33 per cent reservation for women by increasing the number of seats by 50 per cent. It also proposes to freeze the revised seat allocations and constituency boundaries until 2051.

Article Title: President Murmu clears key procedural step for tabling of revised Delimitation Bill in Parliament
Article Text:
File photo: President Droupadi Murmu

Revised package proposes 50% increase in seats

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lok Sabha to sit from November 30

NEW DELHI: President Droupadi Murmu on Saturday recommended that the Lok Sabha consider the Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, under Article 117(3) of the Constitution, completing a key procedural requirement ahead of Parliament's sitting beginning November 30.According to a Lok Sabha Secretariat bulletin, the recommendation followed a communication sent on November 27 by Union minister of state for law and justice and parliamentary affairs Arjun Ram Meghwal to the Lok Sabha secretary-general.Article 117(3) requires the President's recommendation before either House of Parliament can pass a Bill that, if enacted and brought into operation, would involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India.The development comes a day after the Union Cabinet approved a revised legislative package comprising the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, the Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, and the accompanying Union Territories Laws Amendment Bill.The government is expected to withdraw the pending Bills introduced in April, which failed to secure passage after the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha, and introduce the revised drafts on Monday.The revised package proposes a uniform 50 per cent increase in the number of Lok Sabha and state Assembly seats across states and Union Territories.Under the proposal, the Lok Sabha's maximum strength would increase from 550 to 850, while the maximum strength of state Assemblies would rise from 500 to 650.The package also proposes redrawing constituencies within each state based on the latest published Census figures, which would be the 2011 Census, rather than waiting for the 2026-27 Census. The distribution of seats among states would remain frozen until 2051.Another key provision concerns the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state Assemblies. The proposed Delimitation Commission would redraw constituency boundaries in time for the quota to take effect ahead of the 2029 general elections.The Lok Sabha is scheduled to meet from November 30 to December 3, while the Rajya Sabha will reconvene separately on December 2.The revised Bills are expected to be introduced during the sitting, replacing the legislative proposals that failed to clear the Lok Sabha in April.The earlier Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill sought to expand the strength of the Lok Sabha and facilitate the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures. It failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the House.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha to sit from November 30 to December 3. President Droupadi Murmu recommended that the Lok Sabha consider the Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, under Article 117(3) of the Constitution. Union Cabinet approved a revised legislative package.

Article Title: Odisha to host National conference on AI in litigation on December 12-13
Article Text:
On December 12 and 13, Odisha will be the site of a groundbreaking two-day conference focused on artificial intelligence's impact on litigation.

Why is this conference important for India's judicial system ?

Some important areas of technological development include:

Digital courts: Technology is being used to manage case records, filings and court proceedings.

AI-assisted translation: Language technology can help make judgments accessible to people who do not understand English.

Legal research: AI tools can assist legal professionals in searching and analysing large collections of judgments.

Virtual hearings: Digital platforms have expanded access to court proceedings beyond physical courtrooms.

The Odisha government is preparing to host a two-day conference on the use of artificial intelligence in litigation, which is expected to be attended by the chief justice of India and judges from several high courts, officials said on Saturday.The participation of senior judicial officials is expected to make the conference an important platform for discussing technology's growing role in the Indian justice system, reported by PTI.The conference, titled ‘Artificial Intelligence in Litigation - Issues and Challenges’, will be held on December 12 and 13 and is likely to bring together around 300 delegates included senior members of the judiciary, legal experts and other stakeholders to discuss how artificial intelligence can be used in India's justice delivery system, chief secretary Anu Garg said.Garg said the event would serve as an important platform to discuss the growing role of artificial intelligence in the justice delivery system and the challenges associated with its use.She also directed the departments concerned to coordinate closely to ensure the smooth and successful organisation of the conference.The conference is significant because AI is increasingly influencing legal research, case management, documentation, evidence analysis and court administration. At the same time, its use raises questions about accuracy, accountability, data privacy and judicial independence.India's judicial system is increasingly exploring technology to improve access to justice and court administration.
Article Summary: Odisha will host a two-day conference on the use of artificial intelligence in litigation. It is expected to be attended by the chief justice of India and judges from several high courts. The conference is significant because AI is increasingly influencing legal research, case management and documentation.

Article Title: 'Did not prioritise family planning': Javed Akhtar questions seat distribution under delimitation
Article Text:
Akhtar said the final plan was yet to be made public and several aspects of the exercise remained unclear.

NEW DELHI: Lyricist and former MP, Javed Akhtar , on Saturday questioned the Centre's proposed delimitation Bill, raising concerns over the allocation of Lok Sabha seats and the potential disadvantage to states that prioritised family planning.Speaking to the media at an event, Akhtar said the final plan was yet to be made public and several aspects of the exercise remained unclear.“First, the final plan has not yet been revealed, how it will be executed, whether new constituencies will be created, what criteria will be considered, and how the country will be divided into various constituencies,” he said, as per ANI.He also questioned the proposed allocation of seats, arguing that states which had not prioritised family planning could benefit at the expense of those that had.“Second, I find it somewhat strange that regions that did not prioritise family planning are being granted more seats, while those that followed family planning are being allocated fewer seats… How does this create any balance? We will examine the details once they are released… We will also observe which members of the opposition, beyond our own government, come forward to endorse or reject this…” he said.The Union Cabinet has cleared three revised draft legislations to facilitate the proposed delimitation exercise and implementation of women's reservation.These include the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, the Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, and a proposed amendment to laws governing Union Territories. The Bills are scheduled to be taken up during the special session of Parliament beginning November 30.The proposed legislative package provides for a 50% increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats allocated to every state and Union Territory, alongside a corresponding increase in the strength of state legislative assemblies. It proposes raising the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha to 850, with up to 815 members representing states and 35 representing Union Territories.The package also seeks to facilitate the implementation of the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, which provides for 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.While the Opposition has backed women's reservation, it has objected to linking its implementation with delimitation and demanded that the exercise be based on the latest Census data.The Centre has proposed using the 2011 Census for redrawing constituencies and determining seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, while retaining the 1971 population basis for state-wise allocation of Lok Sabha seats until 2051.
Article Summary: Javed Akhtar raises concerns over the allocation of Lok Sabha seats and the potential disadvantage to states that prioritised family planning. Akhtar said the final plan was yet to be made public and several aspects of the exercise remained unclear. The Union Cabinet has cleared three revised draft legislations to facilitate the proposed delimitation exercise and implementation of women's reservation.

Article Title: Widowed woman raises 3 children in matrimonial home for over 25 years after husband's death; Delhi HC says father-in-law cannot evict her until he provides alternative accommodation or pays Rs 25,000
Article Text:
AI Generated Image Used For Representational Purpose Only.





NEW DELHI: A widowed woman who has lived in her matrimonial home for more than 25 years cannot be forced to leave it until her father-in-law arranges another place for her to stay or pays her Rs 25,000 a month towards rent, the Delhi High Court has ruled. The court has upheld the father's claim to ownership of the house, but said the possession order in his favour would remain unenforceable until the woman's housing needs were addressed.While deciding the woman's appeal against a 2024 trial court decree, the high court said the law had to balance the property owner's right to recover his home with the widow's entitlement to residence under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. The woman married on September 11, 2000, and moved into the house with her husband. The couple raised their three children there. After her husband died on May 1, 2016, she continued to live in the property.Her father-in-law, who said the house belonged exclusively to him under a sale deed executed on January 19, 2001, revoked the family's permission to stay through a legal notice in December 2016. His two other sons left the house, but the widow remained.He subsequently filed a suit seeking possession of the ground floor and Rs 25,000 a month in damages for its occupation. The trial court granted him possession in April 2024, but refused damages as he had not provided evidence to establish the amount.The woman appealed, contending that the property was ancestral and that she had a right to remain there as it was her shared household. The high court found no evidence linking ancestral funds to the purchase of the property and rejected her claim on that ground. The sale deed was in her father-in-law's name.However, the court said the ownership documents did not settle the question of her right to residence. Having lived in the house with her husband for nearly 16 years and brought up their children there, the property was their established family home. Under Section 17 of the Domestic Violence Act, a woman's right to reside in a shared household does not depend on whether she owns it. The court said the right was not extinguished by her husband's death or by the father-in-law withdrawing permission for her to stay.It also allowed her to rely on this protection in the appeal, despite not having expressly described the house as a shared household in her written statement. The relevant facts had been pleaded and were not disputed. The court further examined the widow's entitlement to maintenance under Section 19 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956. The provision requires a father-in-law to maintain a widowed daughter-in-law who cannot support herself from her own earnings, property or other specified sources. Such maintenance, the court said, includes a place to live.The woman had studied up to Class 10. The court found no evidence that she had an independent income, property or an estate left by her husband. Her father-in-law pointed to Rs 25.13 lakh she had received in 2016 through execution proceedings arising from an arbitration award in her late husband's favour. The high court clarified that the amount was not Rs 1 crore and did not constitute insurance money.The court said the sum had been received nearly 10 years earlier to support four family members and could not reasonably be expected to fund the woman's housing for the rest of her life. Although the amount was relevant while deciding what the father-in-law should provide, it did not mean she no longer needed shelter. The judge also noted that the relationship between the two had broken down, making it unsuitable for them to continue living together.The possession decree was therefore upheld, but its execution was made conditional. The father-in-law must either provide the woman with suitable alternative accommodation comparable to her existing home or pay Rs 25,000 every month so that she can rent a similar place. The court said the monthly amount was based on the valuation the father-in-law himself had placed on the ground-floor occupation in his suit. It also made clear that the order would not determine either side's claims in the pending partition case, which must be decided separately.
Article Summary: Widowed woman cannot be forced to leave her matrimonial home until her father- in-law arranges another place for her to stay or pays her Rs 25,000 a month towards rent. Delhi High Court has upheld the father's claim to ownership of the house, but said the possession order would remain unenforceable until the woman's housing needs were addressed.

Article Title: PM Modi to hold key cabinet meet at 1 pm; tweaks to delimitation-linked women's quota Bill on agenda
Article Text:
Centre may delink delimitation from Census and consider a 50% seat increase across states.

NEW DELHI: The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, is scheduled to meet on Friday to discuss the delimitation-linked Women's Reservation Bill, ahead of the special sitting of Parliament beginning November 30, sources told ANI.The meeting has been convened at 1 pm at Sewa Teerth, with all ministers asked to ensure their presence. According to new agency ANI, The government is likely to consider amendments to the earlier version of the legislation, which seeks to provide 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.The reported discussions come amid indications that the government is exploring changes to the delimitation framework, including a proposal to increase Lok Sabha seats by 50% across all states and retain their existing inter-state share based on the 1971 Census.According to PTI, the proposed formula is aimed at addressing concerns, particularly among southern states, over the impact of delimitation on their parliamentary representation. However, no final decision has been taken.Some media reports have also suggested that the government may consider delinking delimitation from the Census, potentially allowing the exercise to proceed without waiting for the next Census figures.The special sitting of Parliament is scheduled to begin with the Lok Sabha reconvening on November 30, while the Rajya Sabha will meet from December 2. The sittings are expected to conclude on December 3, subject to government business.The proposed legislation follows the defeat of the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, in the Lok Sabha in April. The bill sought to link the implementation of 33% women's reservation in legislatures with delimitation and proposed increasing the strength of the Lok Sabha from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats.
Article Summary: The meeting has been convened at 1 pm at Sewa Teerth, with all ministers asked to ensure their presence. The government is likely to consider amendments to the earlier version of the legislation, which seeks to provide 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.

Article Title: Cabinet clears bills to raise 50% Lok Sabha seats across states, freeze delimitation till 2051
Article Text:
A third bill will seek to facilitate an increase in the number of seats in the UTs of Delhi, J&K and Puducherry which have assemblies.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Amid growing support for the delimitation bills with support of DMK, the Sharad Pawar-led NCP faction and YSRCP, the Union Cabinet cleared the legislation to increase Lok Sabha’s maximum strength from 550 to 850 by proposing a uniform increase of 50% in constituencies in every state, while freezing any fresh delimitation to revise the numbers till 2051.Government circulated the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill for delimitation and operationalisation of women’s quota from 2029, and another bill for setting up a Delimitation Commission to MPs on Friday as numbers appeared to be falling in place for Parliament’s nod to the government’s centrepiece legislation, only months after a united opposition had voted down the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill with similar objectives.A third bill will seek to facilitate an increase in the number of seats in the UTs of Delhi, J&K and Puducherry which have assemblies.“The objective of the present bill (Constitution amendment) is to give immediate effect to one-third reservation for women, including women belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, in Lok Sabha and legislative assemblies of states and Union Territories, through a delimitation exercise.Such delimitation shall provide for an increase of 50% in the number of seats in Lok Sabha and assemblies of states and Union Territories over and above the number of seats existing immediately before such delimitation,” the Constitution amendment bill said.The new bill is different from its previous version in making an explicit constitutional provision to assuage the concerns of parties like DMK and NCP (SP) of any diminishment of the existing share of states in LS, opening the path for them to junk their past opposition and join the BJP-led NDA in backing the Constitution amendment bill that needs support of two-thirds MPs for passage.For the simultaneous pursuit of the two objectives, the bills have been predicated on the numbers of two Census exercises. For determining the respective share of states in LS, the 1971 Census -- the one which was used for determining the current share of states in LS, is being retained. However, for redrawing the boundaries of LS constituencies in states, the 2011 Census numbers will be used: something which frees the government of the need to wait for the findings of the enumeration currently underway.In the proposed maximum strength of 850 in Lok Sabha, 815 will be for states and 35 for UTs with assemblies -- Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir. The real overall strength of Lok Sabha is likely to be around 816. LS currently has a strength of 543 against the maximum possible strength of 550.The government is set to table the bills, key for implementation of women’s quota, in Lok Sabha on Nov 30. The bills are more granular in their legal casing as well as political outreach, while keeping the same broad agenda of rolling out one-third reservation for women in LS and state assemblies from 2029, when the next national election is due.Signalling his likely change of stand, DMK chief M K Stalin said the share of Tamil Nadu, which has 39 LS seats, should not fall below its current 7.18%, and the existing proportion of parliamentary representation among states, as determined on the basis of the 1971 Census and frozen earlier, must remain unchanged for another 25 years. The government had offered to meet the condition in April itself and the new bill addresses both of Stalin’s points.NCP(SP) was more categorical, with its senior functionary Jitendra Awhad quoting party boss Sharad Pawar to say that the party, an INDIA bloc constituent, had decided to support delimitation.DMK’s 22 MPs in LS, NCP (SP)’s eight and four of YSR Congress, which is also expected to support, takes NDA’s strength in the House to 355. With 360 needed for the bills’ passage in the House, which has three vacancies, NDA appears all but certain to cross the threshold amid indications from the governing alliance that some more MPs may either abstain or even back it.Attention is also focused on whether the speaker will give his ruling on the legality of the split in TMC which has resulted in 20 MPs belonging to Mamata Banerjee’s party aligning themselves with NDA. A favourable ruling will free them from any legal encumbrance in taking an independent course.The Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, which will amend eight Articles of the Constitution, also proposes to raise the ceiling on the size of a state assembly from 500 to 650. It is being explicitly done for Uttar Pradesh as its assembly, the largest in the country, currently has 403 members.Passage of the bill will also provide the government an effective plank to showcase its pro-women credentials in the run-up to a crucial round of state elections, and government is likely to build political capital out of it by getting endorsement from assemblies of states where BJP and its allies are in office.With a new delimitation bill being tabled, government will withdraw the earlier legislation which is still pending in Lok Sabha.
Article Summary: Government circulated the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill for delimitation and operationalisation of women’s quota from 2029. A third bill will seek to facilitate an increase in the number of seats in the UTs of Delhi, J&K and Puducherry which have assemblies.

Article Title: Bisleri in fresh trouble: After Goa, FSSAI finds bacteria in West Bengal water sample
Article Text:
Following the findings, the FSSAI prohibited the sale of a specific batch of the product, numbered PB 201, on August 12.

Second case after Goa plant sample fails test

FSSAI steps up packaged water surveillance

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International after a packaged drinking water sample collected from its plant in West Bengal tested positive for coliform bacteria. This is the second time the food regulator has initiated prosecution against the bottled water major this week, following a similar action over a sample from its Goa plant.West Bengal sample was collected from Bisleri's plant in Telipara village in Jalpaiguri district, news agency PTI reported citing sources. Both the primary and referral laboratories confirmed the presence of coliform bacteria, which can enter water systems through sewage leaks, damaged pipes and other sources.Following the findings, the FSSAI prohibited the sale of a specific batch of the product, numbered PB 201, on August 12. The regulator has now granted sanction for prosecution over violations of food safety rules.Responses from the FSSAI and Bisleri International could not be ascertained immediately.The latest action comes days after the FSSAI announced prosecution proceedings against Bisleri over a sample collected from one of its plants in Goa.In that case, the regulator said the "sample was found non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under the FSS Act, 2006."Bisleri subsequently appealed against the findings, following which the sample was sent to a referral food laboratory. The second laboratory also classified it as "unsafe" after detecting polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), according to the FSSAI.The findings confirmed violations related to unsafe food practices, prompting the regulator to initiate prosecution under the Food Safety Act, 2006.On Monday, Bisleri International maintained that its products were safe for consumption. The company also said it would cooperate with the FSSAI to address the concerns raised.The action against Bisleri comes amid an expanded nationwide crackdown on packaged drinking water quality.FSSAI CEO Rajit Punhani said earlier this week that the regulator was collecting packaged drinking water samples across the country. Laboratory testing is expected to be completed within one to two months.He said the enforcement drive was aimed at ensuring compliance and not creating panic.Punhani also said the regulator had undertaken enforcement activities covering several food and beverage products over the past year. It would soon extend inspections to packaging materials used for food products.The central regulator has also written to state food commissioners and regional directors, asking them to step up surveillance, inspections and sampling of packaged drinking water and mineral water. It has directed them to take action against companies found violating food safety norms.This year, the FSSAI has intensified enforcement against food business operators and e-commerce companies. It has also taken action against manufacturers of energy drinks and alcoholic beverages.
Article Summary: Second case after Goa plant sample fails test for coliform bacteria. Following the findings, the FSSAI prohibited the sale of a specific batch of the product, numbered PB 201. The regulator has now granted sanction for prosecution over violations of food safety rules.

Article Title: E-certificates for new citizens, hard copy on request
Article Text:
Persons acquiring citizenship by naturalisation under Section 6(1) of the Citizenship Act will also be issued a digital certificate of naturalisation in Form XII, signed by an officer authorised by the Centre.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Individuals who acquire Indian citizenship by registration or naturalisation will henceforth only be issued a digital certificate of registration as a citizen, with a hard copy being provided only upon the applicant’s request.As per amendments notified to Citizenship Rules, 2009, every person who is registered as a citizen of India under clauses a, c, d, e or f of Section 5(1) of Citizenship Act — by virtue of marriage to an Indian national, being born to Indian parents, or persons of Indian origin, etc — will be issued a digital certificate of registration in Form X, digitally signed or signed by an officer not under the rank of under-secretary to government of India or one who is authorised by the central government.Persons acquiring citizenship by naturalisation under Section 6(1) of the Citizenship Act will also be issued a digital certificate of naturalisation in Form XII, signed by an officer authorised by the Centre, and must place a request in case they want a hard copy of the certificate.
Article Summary: Individuals who acquire Indian citizenship by registration or naturalisation will henceforth only be issued a digital certificate of registration as a citizen. A hard copy of the certificate will be provided only upon the applicant’s request. Persons acquiring citizenship by naturalisation under Section 6(1) of the Citizenship Act will also be issued an online certificate of naturalisation in Form XII.

Article Title: Watch: Putin hails PM Modi's 'Make in India' vision, praises 16-year-old Indian AI entrepreneur
Article Text:
Putin hails PM Modi's 'Make in India' vision

Putin's praise comes days after US trade body targets 'Make in India'

Who is Raul John Aju, the 'AI Kid of India'?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday praised the work of 16-year-old Indian entrepreneur Raul John Aju, linking his efforts in artificial intelligence (AI) to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ' Make in India ' initiative during the AI Journey 2026 conference. Putin and Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev interacted with young innovators at the conference, where Aju, the founder and chief technology officer (CTO) of AI Realm Technologies, was among those introduced to the Russian president.During the interaction, Putin acknowledged Aju's work and highlighted how young innovators developing their own technological solutions contribute to the objectives of the 'Make in India' initiative."Ultimately your work helps realize PM Modi's "Make in India" call right? Because it helps young people find their own solutions and implement these solutions," Putin told Aju.Putin's remarks come days after the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) criticised India's manufacturing and export policies, including the 'Make in India' initiative, in a report examining structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors.In its Section 301 investigation report into India's acts, policies and practices relating to structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors, the USTR alleged that India had adopted several measures that contributed to excess manufacturing capacity and production while failing to effectively address the resulting global concerns."India engages in a range of acts, policies, and practices that create, maintain, or contribute to the structural excess capacity and production evident in the indicia described above. Key among these are the umbrella efforts of Make in India, PLI, Atmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India), and IBEF, with a particular emphasis on efforts related to or under these efforts in the steel, solar, health, and ICT sectors," the USTR said.The report specifically identified the government's flagship 'Make in India' programme, Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative and India Brand Equity Foundation (IBEF) among the measures it said contributed to structural excess capacity.Popularly known online as 'Raul the Rockstar' and often described as the 'AI Kid of India', Aju is a teenager from Kerala who has pursued artificial intelligence despite coming from a Commerce background rather than a conventional engineering or computer science pathway.According to information shared on his LinkedIn profile, his interest in technology began when he was around nine years old. What started as independent learning and experimentation gradually developed into AI projects, educational initiatives and a growing online community.Aju studied Plus Two Commerce at North Edappally GHSS while simultaneously working on artificial intelligence projects. His LinkedIn profile identifies him as the founder and CTO of AIRealm Technologies, where he develops AI products and practical technology solutions.Projects associated with him include ThinkCraft, RESQ AI and MeBot, among other AI-based tools. He is also associated with ThinkCraft Academy, an AI learning platform that introduces students and professionals to emerging technologies.Beyond developing software, Aju has conducted AI workshops and sessions for students, educators and professionals, with a focus on making the technology accessible to people without technical backgrounds."I build things with AI. I talk about them. Sometimes I break them. Then I build them again," he writes in his LinkedIn introduction.His profile also states that he has delivered eight TEDx talks and conducted sessions at IITs, universities, schools and other institutions. He has built an online following of more than 500,000 people, sharing content related to artificial intelligence and emerging technologies.
Article Summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin praised the work of 16-year-old Indian entrepreneur Raul John Aju. Putin linked Aju's efforts in artificial intelligence to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 'Make in India' initiative. Aju is the founder and chief technology officer (CTO) of AI Realm Technologies.

Article Title: Support to Bill may not automatically lead DMK to NDA, but will open alignment path
Article Text:
BJP and DMK were allies in the 1999 Lok Sabha elections and the regional party was a member of the Atal Bihari Vajpayee-led government before their split in 2003.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: If Congress and DMK could join hands in 2004 after their bitter split where the Sonia Gandhi-led outfit accused the M Karunanidhi government of complicity in the assassination of former PM Rajiv Gandhi and brought down the United Front government in 1998, then anything can happen in politics. Thus said a multi-term DMK MP over the prospect of his party’s widely-expected support to BJP in securing passage of the delimitation bill in Parliament after it was in the vanguard of opposition to the governing party since 2014.While DMK’s support to the bill is unlikely to automatically lead the party to BJP-led NDA but it does open a path for their alignment and offer the national party a fresh opening in Tamil Nadu, which has remained a tough nut for it to crack despite repeated attempts. It certainly weakens the anti-South charge DMK, Congress and others have levelled against BJP.Besides making explicit provision in the bill that the share of every state in Lok Sabha will remain the same and the maximum strength of LS will be frozen till 2051, both concessions aimed at winning over DMK, BJP has of late made subtle moves to dial down its push for legislative measures which had drawn sharp opposition from the Tamil party.This includes a sudden slowdown in the working of two parliamentary committees overseeing Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, which has proposed an apex regulator in place of several for higher education, and a Constitution Amendment Bill, which proposes automatic removal of PM, CMs and ministers detained on criminal charges for 30 continuous days, when they were on the verge of adopting their reports.DMK, which has long championed state autonomy and decried central government’s alleged encroachment on its turf, has been sharply critical of both bills.Both parties have a history of working together. BJP and DMK were allies in the 1999 Lok Sabha elections and the regional party was a member of the Atal Bihari Vajpayee-led government before their split in 2003. Their “secular” opposition to BJP, which then moved closer to DMK’s rival AIADMK, helped them explain away their alliance. DMK’s current challenge is the sudden emergence of Vijay-led TVK as Congress dumped it overnight to help the star actor become chief minister.With DMK out of INDIA bloc, its options are limited. With misgivings persisting in a section of party over joining hands with BJP, which too has been a bitter critic of its anti-Hindutva rhetoric, political compulsions may be the glue for them in the same it worked for DMK and Congress in 2004.
Article Summary: BJP and DMK were allies in the 1999 Lok Sabha elections and the regional party was a member of the Atal Bihari Vajpayee-led government before their split in 2003. DMK’s support to the bill is unlikely to automatically lead the party to BJP-led NDA but it does open a path for their alignment.

Article Title: 50% uniform seats increase, delimitation on 2011 census: What govt's new Bill proposes
Article Text:
The original Delimitation Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha on April 16, 2026.

What changes in the revised Bill

50 per cent uniform increase in seats

NEW DELHI: Days before the special parliamentary session, the government has moved to withdraw the Delimitation Bill, 2026, introduced in the Lok Sabha in April. The Centre has replaced it with a revised version that provides for a 50 per cent increase in the number of seats in Parliament and state and Union Territory assemblies, while seeking to give effect to women's reservation.The reasons for withdrawing the original legislation were outlined in a statement signed by minister of state for law and justice (independent charge) Arjun Ram Meghwal on November 27.The proposed replacement, titled the Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, makes substantial changes to the original legislation, particularly regarding the constitution of the Delimitation Commission, the use of Census figures, the allocation of seats reserved for women and the expansion of legislative representation.The original Delimitation Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha on April 16, 2026, along with the Constitution (One Hundred and Thirty-first Amendment) Bill, 2026, and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026.The three Bills were brought in to facilitate the setting up of a Delimitation Commission to readjust the allocation of seats in the Lok Sabha and state and Union Territory Assemblies and redraw constituency boundaries.However, the Constitution Amendment Bill failed to secure the special majority required under Article 368 of the Constitution when it was put to consideration on April 17. Consequently, the two related Bills were not taken up further and the original Delimitation Bill remained pending in the Lok Sabha.The revised legislation expands the scope of delimitation to include provisions for implementing women's reservation in the Lok Sabha and state and Union Territory assemblies.It also requires the Centre to constitute the Delimitation Commission as soon as possible after the proposed legislation comes into force, instead of setting it up "from time to time", as provided in the original Bill.Another significant change is the use of "latest census figures", defined as the most recent Census figures published on the date the proposed legislation comes into force. This means the 2011 Census would be used if no newer Census figures are published before the legislation takes effect. The Commission will use these figures to readjust seat allocation and redraw territorial constituencies.The revised legislation also provides that seats reserved for women will be allotted through rotation in a manner decided by the Delimitation Commission. It further proposes a 50 per cent increase in the number of seats allocated to each state and Union Territory in the Lok Sabha and the total number of seats in their respective legislative assemblies during the first delimitation exercise after the proposed Constitution (One Hundred and Thirty-second Amendment) Act, 2026, comes into force.The Bill adds that the quota would run for 15 years from the commencement of the 2023 amendment, with Parliament empowered to extend it by law, according to news agency PTI.The government has said the uniform increase would enhance overall representation while maintaining the existing relative distribution of seats among states.The government has proposed withdrawing the original Bill under clause (b) of Rule 110 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Lok Sabha, as the revised legislation substantially alters its provisions.
Article Summary: The government has moved to withdraw the Delimitation Bill, 2026, introduced in the Lok Sabha in April. The Centre has replaced it with a revised version that provides for a 50 per cent increase in the number of seats in Parliament and state and Union Territory assemblies. The revised legislation also seeks to give effect to women's reservation.

Article Title: Delimitation Bill provides for redrawing J&K seats in Pakistan-occupied area after occupation ends
Article Text:
The Bill makes a conditional provision for delimiting J&K Assembly seats in the Pakistan-occupied area if it comes out of occupation

What does the Bill say

NEW DELHI: The Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, listed for introduction in the Lok Sabha, provides for redrawing Jammu and Kashmir assembly constituencies in the part of the region under Pakistan's occupation once the occupation ends. Section 3(4) states that the Election Commission will act as the delimitation commission for the area when it ceases to be under occupation.The provision is conditional and would take effect only if the area is no longer occupied. The Bill uses the phrase "falling under the occupation of Pakistan" and does not use the term "PoK".Also Read| Gerrymandering is the new buzzword amid delimitation debate: What is it and why is opposition worried Under Section 3(4), the Election Commission would take on the role of the delimitation commission for assembly constituencies in the area. This differs from the arrangement proposed for the rest of the region.For other areas, the Bill provides for a separate delimitation commission chaired by a sitting or retired Supreme Court judge. The Chief Election Commissioner or an election commissioner and the state election commissioner would be its members.The provision specifically refers to the Jammu and Kashmir legislative assembly. It does not mention Lok Sabha constituencies in the area.The Bill also does not refer to the 24 assembly seats reserved for the area or clarify whether the proposed 50% increase in seats would apply to them.The government will also introduce the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Second Bill, 2026. It seeks to amend laws governing Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir and Puducherry to align them with the proposed 132nd Constitutional Amendment.The constitutional amendment seeks to implement 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies after a fresh delimitation exercise, alongside a proposed 50% increase in seats.Also Read| No change in LS strength, 25-year seat protection: INDIA bloc's demands on delimitation Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir and Puducherry are the three Union territories with legislative assemblies.The delimitation and Union Territories Bills were first introduced in April along with the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill. The package was intended to operationalise women's reservation from 2029.However, the Constitution amendment Bill failed to secure the required numbers in the Lok Sabha. As a result, the other two Bills could not be taken up for voting.The government will now withdraw the pending Bills and introduce fresh versions on Monday, along with a new Constitution amendment Bill.
Article Summary: The Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, is listed for introduction in the Lok Sabha. It provides for redrawing Jammu and Kashmir assembly constituencies in the part of the region under Pakistan's occupation. Section 3(4) states that the Election Commission will act as the delimitation commission for the area when it ceases to be under occupation.

Article Title: Gerrymandering is the new buzzword amid delimitation debate: What is it and why is opposition worried
Article Text:
The opposition fears delimitation could redraw constituency boundaries in ways that give the BJP an electoral advantage ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha polls

What exactly is gerrymandering

Where did the term come from

Why is the opposition worried about delimitation

Assam: How boundary changes can alter electoral arithmetic

Assam's seats after delimitation

Who decides constituency boundaries in India

Why the seat increase has not settled the debate

The number game in Parliament

What if a party could improve its chances of winning an election simply by redrawing the map? That's the fear driving the opposition's concerns over delimitation. As the Centre prepares to push its legislation, parties are warning that changing constituency boundaries could reshape electoral battles in the BJP 's favour ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha polls. The concern has a name - gerrymandering. It means manipulating electoral boundaries to gain a political advantage.Also Read| No change in LS strength, 25-year seat protection: INDIA bloc's demands on delimitation The concern goes beyond the number of MPs each state will send to Parliament. Even if states retain their existing share of Lok Sabha seats, redrawing boundaries within them could change which voters are grouped together, weaken established political strongholds and alter the outcome in individual constituencies. The opposition fears this could give the ruling party an advantage without changing a single vote or removing anyone from the electoral rolls.Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has accused the BJP of seeking to redraw India's electoral map to its advantage ahead of the 2029 general elections. The concern is that even if states retain their existing relative share of Lok Sabha seats, the way constituencies are carved out within each state could influence which parties and communities have a greater chance of winning.In simple terms, gerrymandering is the practice of drawing constituency boundaries in a way that helps one political party win more seats than its overall support among voters might otherwise allow.There are two common ways this can happen.Packing involves concentrating voters likely to support an opposing party into a small number of constituencies. This allows that party to win those seats by large margins but reduces its influence in neighbouring constituencies.Cracking involves splitting a group of voters across several constituencies so that they become a minority in each. This makes it harder for them to elect candidates representing their preferences.In both cases, no voter needs to be removed from the electoral rolls. The advantage comes from changing how voters are grouped geographically. A party can therefore win a larger share of seats without necessarily securing a corresponding increase in its overall vote share.The word has its origins in the United States in 1812 and is a combination of the name of Massachusetts governor Elbridge Gerry and the word 'salamander'.Gerry signed a bill that redrew the state's senate electoral districts in a way that benefited his Democratic-Republican Party. One of the oddly shaped constituencies was compared to a salamander in a newspaper cartoon published by the Boston Gazette on March 26, 1812. The term 'Gerry-mander' was born.Gerry himself reportedly found the proposal 'highly disagreeable' and lost the next election. His party, however, retained control of the legislature.The term has since come to describe the use of electoral boundary changes as a political tool.Delimitation is not limited to deciding how many parliamentary seats a state should have. It also involves redrawing the boundaries of individual constituencies within states.The opposition's apprehension is that the second part of this exercise could be used to alter electoral arithmetic. By changing which areas and voters fall within a constituency, boundary changes can weaken established political strongholds, divide concentrated voter groups or bring together populations with different voting patterns.This is why the opposition argues that protecting the relative share of Lok Sabha seats allocated to states may not be enough. Even if the overall representation of a state remains unchanged, the distribution of voters across its constituencies could change significantly.The opposition has cited the delimitation exercises in Assam and Jammu and Kashmir to question how constituency boundaries may be redrawn. These examples have become part of its argument for greater transparency and safeguards. However, changes in constituency boundaries or their political consequences do not, by themselves, establish gerrymandering. That would require evidence of deliberate manipulation for electoral advantage.Assam's 2023 delimitation offers an example of how redrawing constituency boundaries can change the political landscape without increasing the total number of seats or removing voters from electoral rolls.The exercise retained the state's 126 assembly seats but changed their distribution and boundaries. Barak Valley's tally fell from 15 to 13, while Barpeta went from eight constituencies to six. The Bodoland Territorial Region gained four seats, taking its total from 11 to 15.The reservation pattern also changed. SC-reserved seats increased from eight to nine and ST-reserved seats from 16 to 19. Goalpara West became an ST-reserved constituency, while Barpeta and Naoboicha were designated SC-reserved seats.The redrawing also altered the concentration of voters across constituencies. According to the figures cited in the delimitation analysis, the number of Muslim-dominated constituencies declined from around 35 to 24. This changed electoral arithmetic in areas where the Congress and the All India United Democratic Front (AIUDF) traditionally had a strong base.The exercise was officially aimed at improving representation and reducing disparities in constituency size. The gap between the smallest and largest constituencies, measured by electors, narrowed from 3.54 times to 3.15 times, though significant differences remained.The Assam example illustrates why the drawing of boundaries matters politically. A constituency can retain its name or number while its voter composition changes, potentially altering the parties and communities that have a decisive influence over its outcome. It does not, on its own, prove that the exercise was gerrymandered.The task is assigned to a high-powered body called the Delimitation Commission. In India, such commissions have been constituted four times under the Delimitation Commission Acts — in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002.The commission's orders have the force of law and cannot be challenged in court. They come into effect on a date specified by the President. Copies are laid before Parliament and the state assemblies concerned, but these legislatures cannot modify the orders.This makes the composition, independence and working of the commission important to the current debate. The Opposition wants assurances that the process will be impartial and that constituency boundaries will not be drawn to benefit the party in power.The Centre's proposed 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats and the assurance that states' existing relative share of seats will be protected address one part of the delimitation debate. But the opposition argues that the absolute difference in representation between states will also matter.Rajya Sabha Leader of Opposition Mallikarjun Kharge has said that retaining the present relative proportion of each state's seats for 25 years would address two of the opposition's concerns, but not its 'first and fundamental concern'."The proposed Constitution Amendment Bill has been unveiled. The 'freeze' for 25 years of the present relative proportion of each State to the total seats of the Lok Sabha will address two of our concerns. However, the Bill does not address the first and fundamental concern. While the relative proportion of each State to the total is important, absolute numbers also matter. The increase of 50% will increase the 'gap' between the Southern States and the other States.The 'gap' will increase from 413 to 620. The enlarged gap will overwhelm the number of MPs of the southern states," he said.The debate, therefore, has two connected but distinct dimensions - how parliamentary representation is distributed among states, and how constituency boundaries are drawn within them. While the first determines the number of MPs a state sends to the Lok Sabha, the second can influence who those MPs are and which voters help elect them.That is why the opposition's questions go beyond the increase in Lok Sabha seats. It wants clarity on the rules, the data and the safeguards governing the redrawing of India's electoral map. At the heart of the gerrymandering debate is a simple question - will delimitation merely redraw constituencies to reflect population and ensure fair representation, or could the new boundaries also reshape the electoral contest in favour of those in power?
Article Summary: Delimitation could reshape electoral battles in the BJP's favour ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha polls. The opposition fears this could give the ruling party an advantage without changing a single vote or removing anyone from the electoral rolls. The word gerrymandering is a combination of the name of Massachusetts governor Elbridge Gerry and the word'salamander'

Article Title: 'Historic blunder': Congress's Imran Masood warns DMK, NCP over delimitation Bill support
Article Text:
Imran Masood objects to the SP's candidate announcements for Saharanpur and Behat as seat-sharing negotiations with the Congress continue

DMK formally backed Bill

NCP (SP) yet to clarify stand

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Imran Masood on Saturday criticised the DMK and the NCP (SP) over reports that they could support the Centre's proposed delimitation Bill, warning that such a move could have serious political consequences for the parties.“This would be a historic blunder for DMK and and for the NCP, such a move could threaten their very existence—it will prove most detrimental to them...” Masood said.His remarks came hours before the DMK formally backed the revised delimitation proposal, with party chief MK Stalin calling it a "major victory" for Tamil Nadu after a three-year struggle to protect the state's share of Lok Sabha seats.The decision was taken at a meeting of DMK MPs chaired by Stalin ahead of the special sitting of Parliament, scheduled to begin on November 30.Also Read| 'Stalin, aka Savarkar 2.0': Vijay's TVK mocks DMK with RSS posts over Centre's delimitation bid Masood also accused the Centre of attempting to manipulate political representation through delimitation and alleged that the government was working to alter the country's constitutional framework.Reacting to the Union Cabinet's approval of the proposed Bill, he alleged that the government had been undermining the Constitution for the past 12 years."Under the pretext of delimitation, they intend to manipulate representation.This has been an ongoing trend for the last 12 years—just yesterday, Justice Gavai even wrote a letter to the President, noting that there is a caste imbalance within the Supreme Court itself. They are consistently working to trample upon the Constitution. You will see that the representation of the most backward communities, Scheduled Castes, and minorities is extremely low in this framework. In reality, they are attempting to alter the very fabric of the nation. The Constitution is the soul of India, and that soul is being tampered with..." he said.The DMK's backing comes after the party opposed an earlier delimitation proposal, arguing that using recent population figures to redraw constituencies could reduce Tamil Nadu's share of parliamentary representation and disproportionately benefit northern states.Stalin said the revised proposal addressed the party's key concerns by providing for a uniform 50% increase in seats across states while retaining Tamil Nadu's existing 7.18% share in the Lok Sabha.Earlier on Friday, Stalin had asserted that Tamil Nadu's existing share of Lok Sabha seats must not be reduced under any circumstances."No change in position, no compromise, the DMK will never compromise on Tamil Nadu's interests; nor will it depart from its principles," Stalin said.Meanwhile, NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule has said she will skip the INDIA bloc meeting scheduled for Saturday, citing the health of her father and party chief Sharad Pawar .Sharad Pawar was admitted to a hospital in south Mumbai on Thursday due to dehydration. Sule said she would remain in Mumbai over the weekend and travel to Delhi on Monday to attend the Parliament session."I will go to Delhi on Monday morning to attend the session," she wrote in her WhatsApp status, PTI reported.Meanwhile, Leader of opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge called for a meeting of opposition floor leaders at his residence in New Delhi to formulate a joint strategy ahead of the proposed legislation.The INDIA bloc put forward three key demands on the proposed delimitation exercise, calling for the existing strength of the Lok Sabha to be maintained, women's reservation to be implemented within the current House strength and the allocation of seats among states to remain unchanged for the next 25 years.This comes before the special sitting of Parliament scheduled to begin on November 30 in the Lok Sabha, while the Rajya Sabha will meet on December 2. The sittings are expected to conclude on December 3, subject to government business.
Article Summary: Congress MP Imran Masood criticises the DMK and the NCP (SP) over reports that they could support the Centre's proposed delimitation Bill. He warns that such a move could have serious political consequences for the parties. Masood also accused the Centre of attempting to manipulate political representation through delimitation and alleged that the government was working to alter the constitutional framework.

Article Title: No change in LS strength, 25-year seat protection: INDIA bloc's demands on delimitation
Article Text:
INDIA bloc's 3 demands on delimitation

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc on Saturday put forward three key demands on the proposed delimitation exercise, calling for the existing strength of the Lok Sabha to be maintained, women's reservation to be implemented within the current House strength and the allocation of seats among states to remain unchanged for the next 25 years.The demands were outlined by the Congress after a meeting of INDIA bloc floor leaders at the residence of party president and Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Mallikarjun Kharge, in New Delhi. Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and several other Opposition leaders attended the meeting to discuss the proposed legislation and formulate a joint strategy ahead of the special session of Parliament beginning November 30.In a post on X, the Congress said the proposed delimitation Bill was discussed at the meeting and reiterated the Opposition's position on the exercise.Also Read| Gerrymandering is the new buzzword amid delimitation debate: What is it and why is opposition worried "Our clear demands are: The current strength of the Lok Sabha should be maintained; Women's reservation should be provided based on the current strength of the Lok Sabha; The current allocation of seats among states in the Lok Sabha should be maintained for the next 25 years," the party said.\Addressing a press conference after the meeting, Kharge said the government was now aiming for "800 paar" by proposing to increase the Lok Sabha's strength to 850, after its earlier electoral slogan of "400 paar" had fallen by the wayside. He alleged that the move was intended to help the ruling party seize and retain power indefinitely.Also Read| EC hikes honorarium for SIR tribunal judges Kharge also accused the government of disregarding the interests of Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in the proposed amendment. He said the number of seats reserved for these communities in each state should be proportionate to their population and argued that the proposed legislation made no provision for increasing the number of SC-reserved seats."Furthermore, the interests of the Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) have been completely disregarded; this is an act of injustice... The number of seats reserved for SCs and STs in any given state must be proportional to their respective populations within that state. Consequently, the number of seats reserved for the Scheduled Castes should increase; however, there is no provision for this in the proposed amendment," he said.Pointing to the upcoming 2026 Census, Kharge questioned why the government had remained silent on using the latest population data for the exercise. He alleged that relying on the latest Census figures would increase the number of seats reserved for SCs and STs in line with their population, but the proposed amendment appeared aimed at denying these communities their "rightful share".Among those who attended the meeting were Congress leaders Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Pawan Khera, KC Venugopal, Syed Nasir Hussain, Pramod Tiwari and Gaurav Gogoi, besides Trinamool Congress MPs Abhishek Banerjee and Derek O'Brien.CPM leader A. Rahim, Rashtriya Samaj Party MP N K Premachandran, National Conference leader Chowdry Mohammad Ramzan, Rashtriya Janata Dal leaders Abhay Kushwaha and Manoj Jha, Samajwadi Party MP Ramji Lal Suman and Indian Union Muslim League leader E T Mohammed Basheer were also present.Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Arvind Sawant, Jharkhand Mukti Morcha leader Baidyanath Ram, who joined online, CPI leader P. Santosh and Independent MP Kapil Sibal attended the meeting. A VCK leader could not participate due to a wedding at his residence.The Nationalist Congress Party-Sharadchandra Pawar (NCP-SP), which has indicated support for the revised delimitation proposals, was absent. The DMK, which has also backed the revised proposals subject to safeguards for Tamil Nadu's representation, did not attend either.The meeting comes amid differences within the Opposition over the proposed legislation. While some regional parties have indicated support for the revised proposals, others have raised concerns about their impact on the representation of states.The ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA), meanwhile, has received a boost after the DMK and NCP-SP indicated support for the revised proposals. The two parties together have 30 Lok Sabha MPs, potentially taking the alliance's estimated strength from around 320 to 350.The DMK, which has 22 Lok Sabha MPs, has backed the proposed 50 per cent increase in parliamentary seats across states but has insisted that Tamil Nadu's existing 7.18 per cent share should not be reduced. DMK MP A Raja has said the party would seek amendments to other provisions if necessary.The NCP-SP, which has eight Lok Sabha MPs, has also indicated support for the revised proposals. Party leader Jitendra Awhad said on Friday that the party had decided to back the delimitation process, describing it as a constitutional requirement. The party had opposed the earlier Bill introduced in April but said it would support the fresh proposal if it provided for a uniform 50 per cent increase in seats.The BJP is confident of securing the required two-thirds majority, banking on support from some parties that opposed the earlier Bill and possible backing from Trinamool Congress MPs who may break ranks.The government would need 360 votes if all 540 sitting members participated in the voting. However, the actual two-thirds threshold would depend on the number of members present and voting. A separate requirement of a majority of the House's total membership would also apply.The Lok Sabha currently has 540 sitting members and three vacancies. If Trinamool Congress MP Kalyan Banerjee's suspension remains in force, 539 members, including the Speaker, could attend the proceedings. The Bill would require 359 votes if all 538 members other than the Speaker voted. The threshold would fall if some members were absent.The Union Cabinet has cleared three revised draft legislations: the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, the Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, and a proposed amendment to laws governing Union Territories. The Bills are scheduled to be taken up during the special session of Parliament beginning November 30.The proposed legislative package provides for a 50 per cent increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats allocated to every state and Union Territory, along with a corresponding increase in the strength of state legislative assemblies. It is also intended to facilitate the implementation of the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, which provides for 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies.The Opposition has backed women's reservation but objected to linking its implementation with delimitation. It has also called for the exercise to be based on the latest Census data.Under the Centre's proposal, the 2011 Census would be used for redrawing constituencies and determining seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, while the 1971 population basis for allocating Lok Sabha seats among states would be retained until 2051.
Article Summary: The demands were outlined by the Congress after a meeting of INDIA bloc floor leaders at the residence of party president and Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Mallikarjun Kharge, in New Delhi. The meeting comes amid differences within the Opposition over the proposed legislation.

Article Title: 'Delimitation Bill won't pass': Congress MP says opposition will 'unite to defend' Constitution
Article Text:
Congress MP Pramod Tiwari says Opposition will unite to defend Constitution

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Pramod Tiwari on Saturday asserted that the proposed delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, would fail to clear Parliament during the upcoming special session beginning November 30. He expressed confidence that Opposition parties would close ranks to “defend the Constitution”, accusing the government of attacking and disrespecting its principles.Tiwari's remarks came as INDIA bloc floor leaders met at leader of opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge's residence in New Delhi to discuss a joint strategy against the Centre's proposed constitutional amendment and delimitation exercise."We are fully confident that when it comes to the Constitution, everyone will unite. As the Constitution is being attacked and disrespected, everyone will also stand with us to defend the Constitution. We are fully confident that it will not pass," Tiwari told news agency ANI.The meeting was attended by Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi, Jairam Ramesh, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and K C Venugopal, besides Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee, Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal, RJD leaders Abhay Kumar Singh and Manoj Jha, CPI MP P Sandosh Kumar, IUML MP ET Mohammed Basheer and RSP MP NK Premachandran, among others.Parties outside the INDIA bloc, including the DMK, AAP and BJD, were also invited but did not attend.Meanwhile, DMK MP A Raja indicated that his party was prepared to support the proposed 50 per cent increase in parliamentary seats across states, provided Tamil Nadu's existing share of representation remained protected.Speaking to ANI after a DMK meeting, Raja said, "Our consistent demand is that the share of 7.18% (seat share in Lok Sabha) should not be altered. Now it is being maintained. Of course, procedural issues are there; we will address them. If necessary, we will give an amendment."The Union Cabinet on Friday cleared three revised draft legislations: the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, the delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, and a proposed amendment to laws governing Union territories.The constitutional amendment proposes increasing the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha to 850, including up to 815 members from states and 35 from Union territories. It also seeks a 50 per cent increase in the number of seats allocated to each state and Union territory, while raising the maximum strength of state assemblies from 500 to 650.The proposed changes are intended to facilitate the implementation of the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, which provides for 33 per cent reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies. The revised seat allocations and boundaries are also proposed to remain frozen until 2051.However, Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal questioned the need for increasing the strength of Parliament to implement women's reservation."At the national level, if this Bill is passed, the number of Lok Sabha seats could increase to around 850. The first question is whether a House of 850 members can function properly," Sibal told reporters ahead of the Opposition meeting."We are ready for women's reservation. They can implement it immediately within the existing 543 seats. So that is not their real objective. Their real objective is to remain in power for the next 30-40 years. And for that, what matters most to them is the delimitation Bill," he alleged.The fresh legislative push comes seven months after the earlier Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha on April 17. It received 298 votes in favour and 230 against, falling 54 votes short of the 352 required.The special session is scheduled to begin on November 30, with the Rajya Sabha reconvening on December 2. The sittings are expected to conclude on December 3.
Article Summary: Congress MP Pramod Tiwari says Opposition will unite to defend Constitution. DMK MP A Raja indicated his party was prepared to support the proposed 50 per cent increase in parliamentary seats across states. Union Cabinet on Friday cleared three revised draft legislations.

Article Title: 'Made promise to Nari Shakti': PM Modi pushes for delimitation Bill after Cabinet nod
Article Text:
PM Modi on Women reservation bill

NEW DELHI: With the Union Cabinet clearing the revised constitutional amendment and delimitation Bills to pave the way for 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state assemblies, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday vowed to overcome all hurdles to their implementation. He also hit out at parties opposing the move, asserting that they would not be able to prevent women from securing greater representation in legislative bodies.Taking to social media platform X, PM Modi shared a video with the caption: "We made a promise to our Nari Shakti and we remain committed to fulfilling it..."In the video, the Prime Minister said the struggle to secure greater political participation for women had continued for decades, adding that he had also been working towards the cause for years."The fight to give Nari Shakti their rightful participation has been going on for decades. For years, I too have been among those making efforts towards this cause. Many women have raised this issue before me. Many sisters have written letters to me, sharing their concerns," PM Modi said.He further said he was aware of the expectations of women across the country and assured them that his government would address obstacles to implementing the quota."I know that the blessings of 100 per cent of the country's Nari Shakti are with us. I assure every woman in the country that we will remove every obstacle that comes in the way of women's reservation. We will ensure that these hurdles are removed," he said."Our morale is high, our courage is unshaken, and our resolve is firm," PM Modi added. He also accused parties opposing women's reservation of attempting to prevent women from securing greater representation in legislative bodies."Parties opposing women's reservation will never be able to stop the Nari Shakti of this country from increasing their participation in Parliament and state assemblies. It is only a matter of time," he said.The Union Cabinet has cleared three revised draft legislations, including the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, and the delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026. The constitutional amendment proposes increasing the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha to 850, comprising up to 815 members from states and 35 from Union territories.The proposal also provides for a uniform 50 per cent increase in parliamentary seats across states and Union territories, alongside an increase in the maximum strength of state assemblies from 500 to 650. The revised allocation of seats between states is proposed to remain frozen until 2051, with the 1971 Census retained as the basis for inter-state seat distribution.The fresh proposal comes after the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha in April.Meanwhile, INDIA bloc leaders met at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence to discuss a joint strategy. Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal questioned the proposed expansion, asking whether an 850-member Lok Sabha could function effectively. He also alleged that the government's objective extended beyond women's reservation.
Article Summary: The Union Cabinet has cleared three revised draft legislations. The constitutional amendment proposes increasing the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha to 850. The proposal also provides for a uniform 50 per cent increase in parliamentary seats across states and Union territories. Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal questioned the proposed expansion, asking whether an 850-member Lok Sabha could function effectively.

Article Text:

Article Title: DMK formally backs Centre's delimitation Bill, Stalin calls it 'major victory' for Tamil Nadu
