NEW DELHI: DMK on Saturday formally backed the Centre's proposed delimitation Bill, with party chief MK Stalin calling the revised proposal a "major victory" for Tamil Nadu The decision was taken at a meeting of DMK MPs chaired by Stalin ahead of the special session of Parliament on November 30. The party said it would support the revised Bill while remaining firm on protecting Tamil Nadu's share of Lok Sabha seats.Stalin said the revised proposal incorporated the party's two key demands raised in its 2024 assembly resolution, after the DMK opposed an earlier version of the Bill.Crucially, it prevents delimitation from being based on recent population figures, which would have disproportionately favored northern states, and instead anchors it to the 1971 census, Stalin said.The revised formula would allow Tamil Nadu's Lok Sabha seats to increase while preserving its existing share of representation in Parliament, thereby protecting the state's political interests for the next 25 years, he added.Sharing the resolution on X, the DMK said, "Resolution passed at the DMK parliamentary members’ meeting ahead of the special session of Parliament: We will protect Tamil Nadu’s representation! We will uphold Tamil Nadu’s rights!"The party's backing comes after the Centre renewed its push to implement women's reservation through a delimitation exercise, with a proposed 50% increase in the number of seats in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies.The DMK had opposed an earlier version of the delimitation proposal, arguing that using recent population figures to redraw constituencies could reduce Tamil Nadu's share of parliamentary representation and disproportionately benefit northern states.The revised proposal, according to the party, addresses its key concerns by providing for a uniform 50% increase in seats across states, while maintaining Tamil Nadu's existing share of 7.18% in the Lok Sabha.The party said the approach would protect the state's political representation for the next 25 years while allowing women's reservation to be implemented.DMK deputy secretary and MP A Raja said the decision was based on the principle of preserving Tamil Nadu's share of seats.Speaking to reporters, Raja said, "We have taken this decision based on the principle that Tamil Nadu's share of 7.18% must remain unchanged... We have agreed on the figure of 59. The DMK President has given us full authority to make any other amendments as may be necessary. When the Congress party was part of our alliance, this was also the demand put forward by the Congress party. A fair delimitation process must continue. On the issue of delimitation, the DMK continues to maintain the same position it held when it was in alliance with the Congress party.""Our consistent demand is that the share of 7.18% (seat share in Lok Sabha) should not be altered. Now it is being maintained. Of course, procedural issues are there; we will address them. If necessary, we will give an amendment," he added.DMK MP Dayanidhi Maran said the party had been demanding a fair delimitation process and that the proposed uniform increase in seats would ensure states do not gain or lose disproportionately."Our demand has been accepted. We want the status quo to prevail. Either there should be no delimitation, or if delimitation is carried out, our rights must be protected. The number of seats for southern states should not be reduced, and northern states should not get disproportionately more seats. Today, Uttar Pradesh is also getting a 50% increase, Bihar is also getting a 50% increase, and Tamil Nadu is also getting a 50% increase. This is the status quo. There is no change. We are ensuring that our rights are protected for the next 25 years, apart from the implementation of women's reservation," he said.Earlier on Friday, Stalin had reiterated that Tamil Nadu's existing 7.18% share of Lok Sabha seats must not be reduced under any circumstances."No change in position, no compromise, the DMK will never compromise on Tamil Nadu’s interests; nor will it depart from its principles," Stalin had asserted.The DMK has maintained that it is not opposed to delimitation but wants the exercise to be fair to all states. In August, it backed a resolution in the Tamil Nadu assembly urging the Centre to freeze the Lok Sabha's existing strength at 543 seats.The DMK's position has assumed significance amid changing political equations in Tamil Nadu following the formation of the TVK government led by Vijay .The DMK had earlier walked out of the INDIA bloc after the Congress extended support to Vijay-led Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) following the Tamil Nadu assembly elections, paving the way for the party to form the government in the state.Meanwhile, leader of opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge has convened a meeting of opposition floor leaders at his residence in New Delhi on Saturday to formulate a joint strategy ahead of the government's likely move to introduce a constitutional amendment bill linked to delimitation.Leaders of opposition parties outside the INDIA bloc, including the DMK, AAP and BJD have also been invited. The opposition is seeking to coordinate its response to the proposed legislation ahead of the special sitting of Parliament, scheduled to begin on November 30.
Article Summary: Party chief MK Stalin calls revised proposal a "major victory" for Tamil Nadu. The party said it would support the revised Bill while remaining firm on protecting Tamil Nadu's share of Lok Sabha seats. The decision was taken at a meeting of DMK MPs ahead of the special session of Parliament.

Article Title: 131st vs 132nd Amendment Bills: What has changed in the Centre's fresh delimitation proposal
Article Text:
Key changes in Centre’s fresh delimitation proposal

Here are the key differences between the two proposals:

Uniform 50 per cent increase in seats for all states and UTs

Key differences in the proposed bills

Use of 2011 Census figures for delimitation

Also Read|

Revised seat allocations and boundaries to remain until 2051

New Delimitation Commission to oversee the exercise

Earlier Bill defeated in Lok Sabha in April

NEW DELHI: Centre is set to introduce the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, in the Lok Sabha on Monday, seeking to implement one-third reservation for women in Parliament and state and Union territory legislative assemblies through a fresh delimitation exercise.The proposed legislation differs from the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, defeated in the Lok Sabha in April, mainly in its approach to delimitation, the allocation of seats among states and the census data to be used for redrawing constituencies.The most significant change in the 132nd Amendment Bill is the provision for a uniform 50 per cent increase in the number of seats in the Lok Sabha and the legislative assemblies of every state and Union territory.The fresh Bill proposes to increase the Lok Sabha's maximum strength to 850, comprising up to 815 members from states and 35 from Union territories. It also seeks to raise the ceiling on the strength of state assemblies from 500 to 650.The earlier 131st Amendment Bill did not provide for a uniform percentage increase in seats across states. Under the fresh proposal, applying the same 50 per cent increase to each state's existing strength would broadly preserve its share of seats in the Lok Sabha.The two proposals also differ in the census data they allow for delimitation.The 2023 women's reservation law linked the implementation of the quota to delimitation after the publication of figures from the first census conducted after the law came into force.The fresh Bill, however, allows constituency boundaries to be redrawn using the "latest published census figures available on the date of the commencement" of the proposed amendment. This effectively means the 2011 Census figures.The 132nd Amendment Bill proposes that the revised allocation of seats and the division of constituencies following delimitation remain in force until 2051.The fresh proposal also provides for one-third reservation for women, including those belonging to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, for 15 years from the commencement of the 2023 amendment. Parliament would have the power to extend the reservation period by law.It would also determine the authority and manner in which seats reserved for women are rotated.The accompanying Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, provides for a three-member commission headed by a serving or former Supreme Court judge appointed by the Centre.The commission would determine the allocation of seats, redraw constituencies and identify seats to be reserved for women.Under the Bill, reserved seats would be allotted by rotation "as the Commission may deem fit". Seats reserved for women from the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes would be rotated within constituencies reserved for their respective categories.The earlier Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha on April 17, falling short of the required two-thirds majority. A total of 298 MPs voted in favour of the Bill, while 230 voted against it.The government subsequently did not proceed with the accompanying Bills.
Article Summary: The Centre is set to introduce the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, in the Lok Sabha on Monday. It seeks to implement one-third reservation for women in Parliament and state and Union territory legislative assemblies through a fresh delimitation exercise. The proposed legislation differs from the earlier Constitution (131st Amendment), defeated in Lok Sabha in April. The most significant change is the provision for a uniform 50 per cent increase in the number of seats.

NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra Pradesh Congress Committee on Saturday criticised its ally, the Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar), over its decision to support the BJP-led Centre's proposed delimitation exercise, recalling how the Congress had set aside its claim to a Rajya Sabha seat earlier this year to facilitate the re-election of party chief Sharad Pawar In a post on X, the Maharashtra Congress reminded Sharad Pawar and NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule that the Congress had backed the 85-year-old leader's candidature for the Upper House despite having a claim to the seat."The Congress party had stood firmly behind Sharad Pawar right to the end to send him back to the Rajya Sabha at the age of 85. Elections were due to be held in March 2026 for Maharashtra’s 7 Rajya Sabha seats. The Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) had just 10 MLAs. A candidate needed 36 votes to get elected. Congress had 16 MLAs, while Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray) had 20," it said.The state Congress further claimed that Supriya Sule had personally approached senior Congress leaders seeking their support for her father's nomination. It said Rahul Gandhi and party president Mallikarjun Kharge had agreed without hesitation, following which the Congress gave up its claim to the seat.The Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray) also backed Pawar, and the Maha Vikas Aghadi unanimously endorsed his candidature.Questioning the NCP (SP)'s latest position, the Maharashtra Congress said the party was now preparing to support the BJP government's delimitation proposal."Supriya Sule sought Congress leaders’ support for Sharad Pawar’s candidacy. Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge agreed without any hesitation. Congress set aside its claim to its own seat and supported Sharad Pawar’s candidacy. Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray) then also backed him, and the Maha Vikas Aghadi unanimously confirmed his candidacy. And now what? Against the backdrop of the delimitation law, the same Sharad Pawar, Supriya Sule and their Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) are going to support the BJP government," it said.The Congress criticism followed NCP (SP) leader Jitendra Awhad's announcement on Friday that the party would support the proposed delimitation exercise after discussions with Sharad Pawar.Clarifying the nature of the deliberations, Awhad said the discussions were not initially about the party's official position but focused on delimitation as a constitutional requirement. He subsequently confirmed that the party had decided to back the process."The discussion wasn't about our party's official stance. The general point being made was that the delimitation process is a constitutional requirement... A decision has been made to support the delimitation process, and we will indeed support it. We will support the delimitation," he told reporters.Reacting to the announcement, Maharashtra Congress spokesperson Sachin Sawant expressed surprise at the NCP (SP)'s decision and said Sharad Pawar's political journey had been associated with secular and democratic values.Speaking to news agency PTI, Sawant said the decision should have been discussed at a meeting of the INDIA bloc, stressing the need for opposition unity and collective decision-making."Whether the NCP (SP) decision was taken under pressure or was driven by political calculations will become clear with time," he said.Sawant also questioned the Centre's intentions behind the proposed legislation, alleging that it was aimed at strengthening the government's hold on power. He questioned the rationale for undertaking delimitation in the absence of a fresh Census."This is called gerrymandering. There is no doubt that the government intends to replicate this experiment at the national level," he claimed.Gerrymandering refers to the deliberate manipulation of constituency boundaries to give a political party an electoral advantage.The proposed Delimitation Bill seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from the existing 543 seats to 850, with 815 seats allocated to states and the remaining 35 to Union Territories.The political debate over the legislation has intensified ahead of the special sitting of Parliament. Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju has said the government requested Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and Rajya Sabha Chairman C P Radhakrishnan to reconvene the Houses from November 30 and December 2, respectively, to transact essential government business.Meanwhile, the NCP (SP) has issued a whip directing all its Lok Sabha MPs to remain present in the House from November 30, amid discussions over the numbers required to pass the constitutional amendment linked to delimitation.The party has eight MPs in the Lok Sabha. A constitutional amendment requires a special majority of two-thirds of members present and voting.With five vacancies in the 543-member House, its effective strength stands at 538, putting the two-thirds threshold at approximately 359 votes.
Article Summary: NCP (SP) confirms support for delimitation. Maharashtra Pradesh Congress Committee criticises its ally. Congress had set aside its claim to a Rajya Sabha seat earlier this year to facilitate re-election of party chief Sharad Pawar. Congress criticises NCP (SP)'s latest position.

Article Title: Attacks on shipping, seafarers unacceptable: EAM

NEW DELHI: Attacks on maritime shipping and seafarers are simply unacceptable and call for a global response, EAM S Jaishankar said Friday. Addressing the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA), an inter-governmental body comprising 23 member-states, he said international law, particularly United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, must be respected.The 25th meeting of the IORA council of ministers here was followed by a joint communique that expressed concern over the undermining of maritime safety and security of vessels and seafarers and called for ensuring their safety and security.PM Narendra Modi met the foreign ministers and heads of delegation of the 23 IORA member-states participating in the meeting. “Indian Ocean has connected our people for a millennia. As chair of IORA, India looks forward to working closely with all partners to advance its vision of Mahasagar (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) and to strengthen peace, security, stability and prosperity in the Indian Ocean Region,” he posted on X.According to the Delhi communique, IORA reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining the Indian Ocean as a region of peace, stability and prosperity, and to upholding applicable international law to ensure “freedom of navigation and overflight, unimpeded commerce, peaceful settlement of disputes and other lawful uses of the sea”.It also reaffirmed its commitment to sovereign equality, territorial integrity, political independence, non-interference in internal affairs, peaceful co-existence and mutual benefit.India announced a grant of $500,000 for the association’s institutional and financial capacity-building. “Whether it is to counter terrorism, narcotics trade or illegal, unreported, unregulated fishing, or indeed response to climate events and disaster situations, we have to become more self-reliant as well as more enthusiastic about cooperating with partners,” said Jaishankar.“We are focused on the volatile aspects of a transforming global order, especially conflicts, frictions and disruptions. It is equally imperative to appreciate the promising aspects: deep interdependence, strong globalisation and the benefits of international cooperation,” he said.The Indian Ocean is central to global trade, energy security, connectivity and economic prosperity. It is also a region of immense diversity, opportunity and of shared challenges, he stressed. “Our collective responsibility is to ensure that it remains peaceful, stable, secure and conducive to development,” Jaishankar added.
Article Summary: EAM S Jaishankar has called on Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) nations to deepen collaboration, ensure maritime safety and security. Article Title: J&K gets advocate general after 2 years

Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor (L-G) Manoj Sinha on Friday approved the appointment of senior advocate Syed Faisal Qadri as the Advocate General of the Union Territory (UT), officials said.

SRINAGAR: Senior advocate Syed Faisal Qadri was appointed the advocate general of J&K on Friday, filling a key constitutional post that had remained vacant for two years. Article Title: Masking number plates to evade FASTag? Face six times the toll

NEW DELHI: Vehicle owners now face the risk of paying six times the applicable toll for tampering with or masking a vehicle number plate to evade toll payment at barrier-less or MLFF toll plazas on national highways and expressways. Road transport ministry on Friday directed NHAI to start a pilot implementation of the penalty and create awareness among users to stop such violations.TOI on Nov 22 had first reported the ministry's move to impose heavy penalties -- four to eight times -- on such vehicle owners. In a letter to NHAI, the ministry flagged that certain vehicle users are resorting to deliberate masking, tampering with or concealing vehicle registration numbers to avoid paying toll.It has asked the highways authority to establish the mechanism to use additional details from Vahan database and adjacent toll plaza to identify such vehicles. “Additionally, AI-based image processed data comparing the PUCC image data in Vahan with MLFF vehicle image data may be attempted. This will help to identify and address cases where vehicle registration numbers displayed on the front/ rear of vehicles are deliberately masked, tempered with or concealed and where FASTag also could not be detected,” the ministry said.The penalty will be imposed only when it is established that the violation was deliberate and intended to evade toll payment, the ministry has said. The toll operators will pass on the penalty collections to NHAI.The measure is aimed at preventing toll evasion under the barrier-less electronic toll collection system, which uses FASTag readers and Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras mounted on overhead gantries to identify vehicles and automatically deduct the applicable fee without requiring them to stop.MLFF tolling is being introduced to eliminate physical toll booths and barriers on NHs for seamless travel of vehicles.
Article Summary: Number plate tampering to evade highway tolls will attract heavy penalties. Road transport ministry on Friday directed NHAI to start a pilot implementation of the penalty. The measure is aimed at preventing toll evasion under the barrier- less electronic toll collection system.

Article Title: India looking at investments of Rs 200 lk cr in power sector over next 20 yrs: Power minister
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Union minister Manohar Lal on Friday urged states to join hands with the Centre to expand the transmission network, ramp up nuclear energy production and improve the financial health of distribution companies (discoms), as India looks at investments of Rs 200 lakh crore in the power sector over the next two decades.Speaking at a conference of power ministers of states and Union Territories (UTs), Lal said the sector would need investments of Rs 200 lakh crore until 2047 to achieve various targets and called for stock market listings of state-owned companies and greater participation from private players to mobilise funds.“We cannot do this investment alone. We need investments from the public and list our public sector firms. We also need investment from the private sector under the public-private partnership,” he said.Expressing concern over the cumulative losses of Rs 7 lakh crore incurred by discoms, Lal said the Centre had absorbed a similar amount under the Ujjwal Discom Assurance Yojana (UDAY) in 2017. While discoms earned nearly Rs 2,600 crore in profit in the last fiscal, he said the challenge was to sustain the turnaround through policy, operational and regulatory changes.With India expected to have nearly 530 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2030, Lal flagged the shortage of transmission infrastructure to evacuate green power, particularly solar energy, and stressed the need for the Centre and states to work together to address the challenge.“It is not a good situation that there is huge generation of power but there is a lack of transmission network to evacuate that,” he said.He said power demand would rise with the expansion of data centre infrastructure and increased use of electric vehicles, underlining the need to develop energy storage capacity for optimum utilisation of solar and other renewable sources. Lal also said states had offered 25-30 locations for nuclear projects and urged them to identify more sites to support India’s growing energy requirements.He also urged states to promote solar power in agriculture and through rooftop installations, and advocated the use of advanced technologies such as prepaid smart meters and AI tools to improve power distribution.States such as Haryana, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Himachal Pradesh, along with the UTs of Delhi, Ladakh and Jammu & Kashmir, held closed-door meetings with the power ministry and other agencies. Lal emphasised upon the resource adequacy plan to meet the rising demand of electricity. India recorded a peak power demand of 271 GW in May this year, which is expected to touch 300 GW next year.The conference will deliberate on energy storage deployment, transmission constraints and the financial viability of discoms, besides issues related to nuclear sites. Besides presentations by other states, it will have a joint session involving electricity regulatory commissions and power departments of all states and UTs on Saturday.
Article Summary: Power minister Manohar Lal has said India's power sector will require investments of around ₹200 lakh crore by 2047. Lal flagged the shortage of transmission infrastructure to evacuate green power, particularly solar energy. He also urged states to promote solar power in agriculture and through rooftop installations.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov has described India's ties with Moscow as a "privileged strategic partnership", highlighting the country's importance alongside China and Iran as Russia looks to strengthen its international partnerships amid a shift towards a multipolar world order.Speaking at a meeting with participants of the Alexander Gorchakov Public Diplomacy Fund's Dialogue for the Future programme in Moscow on Thursday, Lavrov said Russia continued to have strong partners despite deteriorating relations with Western countries."Our relations with India are officially described as a privileged strategic partnership. We also enjoy an especially advanced strategic partnership with the Islamic Republic of Iran, formalised in a treaty signed a year and a half ago," he said, as quoted by ANI.Referring to ties with Beijing, Lavrov said the Russia-China partnership had demonstrated its effectiveness at the recently concluded Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, including through the first-ever trilateral summit involving Russia, China and the United States.He also pointed to Russia's wider network of partnerships through groupings such as BRICS, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) and the Collective Security Treaty Organisation (CSTO)."We have no shortage of partners with whom to work," Lavrov said, describing BRICS as a "broad-based association of truly global reach".His remarks come amid continued diplomatic engagement between India and Russia over bilateral ties as well as the Ukraine conflict. Earlier this month, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said India had held discussions with Russia, Ukraine and European countries on three key issues arising from the war: protecting civilian shipping and seafarers, restoring grain exports through the Black Sea and preventing attacks on energy infrastructure.Speaking on the sidelines of the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, Jaishankar said India was attempting to bring the concerned parties together to find common ground on these issues.He stressed that civilian vessels and seafarers should not be targeted and called for restoring grain shipments from both Russia and Ukraine, warning that exports through the Black Sea had declined sharply.On energy infrastructure, Jaishankar said reaching an understanding would be particularly complicated because countries had different interpretations of what needed protection, ranging from refineries and electricity grids to ships carrying fuel.Meanwhile, Lavrov also talked about Moscow's strategic relationship with Tehran. Russia and Iran signed a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty in January 2025, covering cooperation in areas including trade, energy, science, technology and defence. The agreement entered into force in October that year.Making a broader assessment of global power dynamics, Lavrov said the traditional Western-dominated world order was giving way to new centres of economic and political influence."It is obvious to everyone that the issue concerns the tectonic shifts that are underway on the international stage, where the old world order, which was maintained for 500 years, first by Europeans and subsequently by the 'collective West,' is being replaced with new growth centres," he said.Describing multipolarity as an inevitable historical process, Lavrov argued that countries attempting to delay the transition would eventually have to engage with emerging centres of influence."Those who are trying to slow down this process can possibly hinder the rise of the new multipolar world order, but this will eventually take place anyway, and they will have to find common ground," he said.Taking aim at Western countries, he added that the United States, Europe and their allies could no longer dictate how other nations should conduct their international relations or decide whom they should cooperate with.Lavrov said Russia would continue to work through multilateral platforms, including the United Nations and the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), while implementing decisions reached collectively.
Article Summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov has described India's ties with Moscow as a "privileged strategic partnership" His remarks come amid continued diplomatic engagement between India and Russia over bilateral ties as well as the Ukraine conflict. Lavrov also highlighted the country's importance alongside China and Iran as Russia looks to strengthen international partnerships.

Article Title: Maximum assembly seats capped at 650, rotational reserved seats for women: What's in new delimitation bill
Article Text:

What is in the new Bill

The Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, proposes to increase the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha to 850, with up to 815 members from states and 35 from Union territories.

It also proposes to raise the maximum strength of a state legislative assembly from 500 to 650.

It further proposes a 50% increase in the number of seats in the Lok Sabha and state and Union territory assemblies over their existing strength before the delimitation exercise.

The Bill provides that the women's quota will remain in force for 15 years from the commencement of the 2023 amendment, with Parliament empowered to extend it through legislation.

Parliament will also decide the authority and manner in which seats reserved for women will be rotated.

Another key change is that the Centre will have to constitute the Delimitation Commission as soon as possible after the proposed legislation comes into force. The original Bill provided for setting up the commission "from time to time".

The fresh Bill seeks to enable the rollout of the women's quota after the first delimitation exercise under the proposed amendment. The exercise will use the latest Census figures published by the time the law comes into force.

This means the 2011 Census data will be used if no newer figures are published by then. The Delimitation Commission will use these figures to readjust seat allocations and redraw territorial constituencies.”

NEW DELHI: The Centre has proposed increasing the number of Lok Sabha seats by 50% for every state and Union territory, along with a similar increase in the strength of their legislative assemblies, to implement one-third reservation for women.This is the Centre's second attempt to push the legislation after its earlier proposal was defeated in the Lok Sabha in April this year.The earlier three Bills were introduced to facilitate the setting up of a Delimitation Commission to readjust the allocation of seats in the Lok Sabha and state and Union territory assemblies, besides redrawing constituency boundaries.The fresh Bill, set to be introduced in the Lok Sabha on Monday, makes substantial changes to the original legislation, particularly in the constitution of the Delimitation Commission, the use of Census figures, the allocation of seats reserved for women and the expansion of legislative representation."The objective of the present Bill is to give immediate effect to one-third reservation for women, including women belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, in the House of the People and the Legislative Assemblies of the states and the Union territories, through a delimitation exercise," the Bill's Statement of Objects and Reasons says.
Article Summary: The Centre has proposed increasing the number of Lok Sabha seats by 50% for every state and Union territory. It also proposes a similar increase in the strength of their legislative assemblies. This is the Centre's second attempt to push the legislation after its earlier proposal was defeated in the Lok Sabha in April.

Article Title: 'Pressure or political calculation?' Congress questions NCP-SP's decision to back delimitation Bill
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Congress on Friday termed the NCP (SP)'s decision to back the Centre's delimitation Bill "unfortunate", saying that such a decision should have been taken at the INDIA bloc meeting.Reacting to NCP (SP) leader Jitendra Awhad's statement, Maharashtra Congress spokesperson Sachin Sawant expressed surprise at the decision and said that Sharad Pawar 's political journey had been associated with secular and democratic values.Asserting the importance of opposition unity and collective decision-making, Sawant told news agency PTI, "Whether the NCP (SP) decision was taken under pressure or was driven by political calculations will become clear with time."Sawant also said that the government's intention behind the Bill was not genuine and that it was aimed at further tightening its grip on power. He also questioned the rationale behind the proposed exercise in the absence of a fresh Census."This is called gerrymandering. There is no doubt that the government intends to replicate this experiment at the national level," Sawant claimed.Gerrymandering is the deliberate manipulation of constituency boundaries to give a political party an unfair advantage.This comes after NCP (SP) leader Jitendra Awhad said that the party had decided to support the Centre's proposed delimitation Bill, which is set to be tabled during the special session of Parliament.Awhad said that a consensus was reached after discussions with Sharad Pawar, adding that the delimitation process is a constitutional requirement."The discussion wasn't about our party's official stance. The general point being made was that the delimitation process is a constitutional requirement," Awhad said."A decision has been made to support the delimitation process, and we will indeed support it. We will support the delimitation," he added.Meanwhile, Shirur MP Amol Kolhe, the party's whip in the Lok Sabha, said any decision would be taken only after studying the Bill. "Sule had made the party's stand clear. We have to first study the draft of the Bill, only then any decision can be taken," he said.Earlier in the day, Sule said that she would not attend the INDIA bloc meeting scheduled for Saturday to discuss the Opposition's floor strategy for the special Parliament session, as her father Sharad Pawar was ailing."I will go to Delhi on Monday morning to attend the session," she said in her WhatsApp status message.The NCP (SP) also issued a whip directing its Lok Sabha MPs to remain present in the House from November 30. The NCP (SP), which has eight Lok Sabha MPs, took this stand amid discussions on the numbers needed to pass a constitutional amendment linked to delimitation.Such legislation requires a special two-thirds majority of members present and voting.Factoring in five current vacancies in the 543-member House, the effective strength stands at 538, putting the two-thirds threshold at approximately 359 votes.
Article Summary: NCP (SP) leader Jitendra Awhad said that the party had decided to support the Centre's proposed delimitation Bill. Maharashtra Congress spokesperson Sachin Sawant expressed surprise at the decision and said that Sharad Pawar's political journey had been associated with secular and democratic values.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Travis Kelce's $5.35 million Ohio mansion carries a $120,000 tax bill, with $72,000 potentially benefiting local schools
Article Text:
Travis Kelce mansion (Getty Images)

Travis Kelce's Ohio mansion could generate $120,000 in annual property taxes

Travis Kelce's mansion could bring an unexpected boost to Cleveland schools

Travis Kelce's return to Ohio has brought more than a multimillion-dollar mansion into the spotlight. His $5.35 million estate in Bratenahl could also have a financial impact on the community surrounding it. While the Kansas City Chiefs star's sprawling property reflects the success he has built through his NFL career, its estimated annual property tax bill carries an unexpected connection to public education. A significant portion of that money could support Cleveland's public schools, giving the luxury purchase a community angle beyond its impressive price tag.Owning a historic estate comes with responsibilities that extend well beyond its purchase price. For Kelce, those costs could include an estimated $120,000 in property taxes every year, according to an Axios report published in September 2026.The figure offers another perspective on the financial commitment behind the NFL star's Ohio residence. According to Axios Cleveland, the mansion, which reportedly spans approximately 21,000 square feet, is among the most striking residential properties in the Cleveland area.However, its size and value also mean that it could make a substantial contribution to local tax revenues.What makes the estimate particularly interesting is how that money could be distributed. Around 60% of the annual property tax bill, or approximately $72,000, could go towards the Cleveland Metropolitan School District.That is a notable amount for a single residential property to potentially contribute towards public services. It also highlights how high-value real estate can play a role in supporting communities through local taxation.The potential school funding connection adds another dimension to Kelce's investment in his home state. Cleveland Metropolitan School District serves students across the area, and property taxes form an important part of the funding structure supporting public education.Although Kelce's mansion is located in Bratenahl, the village falls within the Cleveland school district. This creates an interesting link between the property and the educational system serving the wider community.The estimated $72,000 allocation is not a personal donation from Kelce or a charitable contribution announced by the football star. Article Title: In 2018, railway crossing barrier snapped and fell on 23-year-old woman’s motorcycle, leaving her permanently 50% disabled; 8 years later, Allahabad HC orders Railways to pay Rs 26.70 lakh compensatio

LUCKNOW: The Allahabad high court has directed the Indian Railways to pay Rs 26.70 lakh compensation to a woman who suffered permanent disability after a railway level-crossing barrier snapped and fell on her motorcycle at Hempur railway crossing in Sitapur district in 2018.A division bench comprising Justice Shekhar B Saraf and Justice Abdhesh Kumar Chaudhary allowed a writ petition filed by Nidhi Devi Mishra, quashed the Railways' orders restricting her compensation to an ex-gratia payment and directed payment of the amount within four weeks.The court also directed the Railways to pay interest at 6% per annum on Rs 16.70 lakh, comprising compensation for loss of future earning capacity and medical expenses, from the date of filing of the present writ petition until payment. In case of default beyond four weeks, interest at the same rate will be payable on the entire compensation amount.The accident occurred on April 8, 2018, when Mishra, then 23, was returning from her D.El.Ed classes as a pillion rider on a motorcycle. After a goods train passed and the crossing gates were raised, the barrier snapped and fell on her. She suffered traumatic paraplegia following a spinal cord injury and was assessed to have 50% permanent disability.The court noted that Mishra, who was pursuing a master's degree in sociology and working as a teacher, had been compelled to approach the High Court repeatedly after the Railways initially rejected her claim, later described her injury as self-inflicted and eventually offered only Rs 25,000 as ex-gratia compensation.Holding that the accident resulted from faulty functioning of the railway barrier, the bench said the Railways could not shift responsibility to the victim. It observed that maintenance of level crossings was a safety responsibility and not a sovereign function.The court held that constitutional courts could award compensation under Article 226 where negligence by a state instrumentality infringed Article 21 and no effective statutory remedy was available.Assessing compensation, the bench considered her notional annual income, future prospects, multiplier and functional disability. It awarded Rs 14.20 lakh for loss of earning capacity, Rs 2.50 lakh towards medical expenses and Rs 10 lakh for pain, suffering, future treatment and loss of amenities.The court clarified that the earlier Rs 46,250 ex-gratia payment would not be adjusted against the compensation. It declined her alternative plea for a railway job, observing that public employment requires a statutory or contractual entitlement.

Article Title: Cold coffee, cigarettes and food orders: 'Cyber trap' that didn't look like one
Article Text:
Delhi Police dismantled a cyber fraud syndicate operating from Noida (AI image)





NOIDA: Foreign nationals allegedly coerced to work out of a bogus Noida-based company whose job was to execute cyber frauds did not show any visible signs of distress, according to staff and vendors at Sovereign Corporate Tower in Sector 136.They didn't look suspicious, would go out for a smoke and cold coffee outside the building, and return to work, they told TOI a day after Delhi Police busted the alleged cyber fraud syndicate operating out of the eighth floor of the 18-storey building and rescued 92 Indonesian and 72 Malaysian nationals.Guards at the facility said the employees of SKV, the name under which the syndicate operated for two and a half months, gave them a hard time, placing frequent orders on Swiggy and Zomato, and asking them to collect the food.The owner of a tea shop just outside the building said the foreign nationals were his regular customers and would frequently step out for cigarettes and cold coffee. Their movements appeared unrestricted, he said. "Nothing about their routine suggested they were being held against their will." Employees of other offices - at least 10-11 companies are operating on the premises - said the foreign nationals appeared to be regular office workers, were frequently seen outside the building and interacted normally with people nearby.Building reception staff said three to four security guards were assigned to accompany some foreign employees after they were involved in a dispute with an employee of another company before Diwali. There were no other restrictions, they claimed. According to police, the foreign nationals arrived in India three to four months ago on six-month business visas. They stayed at a company-provided PG accommodation, Sykhomes, in Shahpur village in Sector 128 and were ferried to and from the call centre in a fleet of about 40 cabs. Shopkeepers in the area also told TOI that the foreign nationals regularly stepped out to buy daily essentials and refreshments, and did not show no visible signs of fear or stress . Neighbours said they roamed the streets and spoke on the phone in their native language."All we knew was they were here working for a foreign company. They never created any trouble. No one in the area suspected them of being involved in such activities," a resident of the area said.Delhi Police said the bogus operation, headed by a Malaysian man, Tan Guan Wei, allegedly used fraudulent online platforms, websites and APK-based applications to cheat unsuspecting people through fake investment schemes. The modus operandi involved creating fictitious identities of women and online profiles to approach people through social media and other platforms.The operators allegedly developed online relationships, gained the trust of strangers and compelled them to invest money through fraudulent trading and investment platforms that promised high returns. They seized 355 mobile phones, 168 desktop computers, 26 laptops, 53 SIM cards and 174 passports from the spot. On Friday, police said the recruits of the bogus call centre were allegedly trained in Malaysia and Cambodia before being brought to India. Once in Noida, they were made to work 15-hour shifts daily, faced pressure to meet financial targets and were restricted from using mobile phones.Noida police, however, said none of the foreign nationals had complained of torture or being forced to work against their will, but were examining how they were recruited and accommodated. An FIR was registered at Sector 126 police station against PG owner Bhram Singh Chauhan and his son Deepanshu for allegedly failing to submit Form C, a mandatory document for reporting the stay of foreign nationals to authorities. The case has been registered under Sections 8 and 23 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025.
Article Summary: Foreign nationals allegedly coerced to work out of bogus Noida-based company. Their job was to execute cyber frauds, according to staff and vendors at Sovereign Corporate Tower in Sector 136. Delhi Police busted the alleged cyber fraud syndicate operating out of the eighth floor of the 18-storey building and rescued 92 Indonesian and 72 Malaysian nationals.
